questions.question: Madhav purchased an item for ₹42,000 and sold it at a loss of 20%. With remaining amount, he purchased another item and sold it at a gain of 30%. What is the overall gain (in ₹)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Successive percentage change formula: Net % Change = x + y + (x × y)/100

⇒ Net % Change = −20 + 30 + (−20 × 30)/100

⇒ Net % Change = 10 − 6 = +4% (Overall Gain)

⇒ Overall Gain = 4% of ₹42,000 = (4/100) × 42000 = ₹1680

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1680.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/332090cb051f59f72072037fb86b1d2fc9cd513bd5fa5215d13a73adc0cd7b3c.png] 

**Given:**

Initial Cost Price = ₹42,000

Loss on the first sale = 20%

Gain on the second sale = 30%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Selling Price of first item = 42000 × (100 − 20)/100

⇒ Selling Price of first item = 42000 × 0.80 = ₹33,600

⇒ Since the new item is bought with the remaining amount, New Cost Price = ₹33,600

⇒ Selling Price of second item = 33600 × (100 + 30)/100

⇒ Selling Price of second item = 33600 × 1.30 = ₹43,680

⇒ Overall Gain = Final Selling Price − Initial Cost Price

⇒ Overall Gain = 43680 − 42000 = ₹1680

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1680.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is sequentially changed by a% and then by b%, the net percentage change is given by: Net % = a + b + (a × b)/100. Use a positive sign for gains/increments and a negative sign for losses/decrements.

Base Value in Profit and Loss

In any business transaction, profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the initial Cost Price (CP) unless explicitly stated otherwise.

Multiplying Factor Method

To directly calculate the final amount after multiple percent changes, use multiplying factors. Final Value = Initial Value × (1 ± x/100) × (1 ± y/100).

questions.question: What is the volume (in cm³) of a cylinder if the radius of the cylinder is 8 cm and the height is 14 cm? (Take 𝝿 = 22/7)
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the volume formula uses π (22 ÷ 7), the final answer must be a multiple of 11.

We check the given options using the divisibility rule for 11 (difference of sums of alternating digits):

Option 1: 2686 → (6 + 2) − (8 + 6) = 8 − 14 = −6 (No)

Option 2: 2816 → (6 + 8) − (1 + 2) = 14 − 3 = 11 (Yes)

Since only 2816 is exactly divisible by 11, it is the correct volume.

**∴ The correct answer is 2816 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of cylinder (r) = 8 cm

Height of cylinder (h) = 14 cm

**Formula Used:**

Volume of cylinder = π × r² × h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e87ff64fe0a7ab5045e3c90346ead7a22deb42f9361dd6dc5c2a648141b49565.png] 

**Calculation:**

⇒ Volume = (22 ÷ 7) × 8² × 14

⇒ Volume = 22 × 64 × (14 ÷ 7)

⇒ Volume = 22 × 64 × 2

⇒ Volume = 44 × 64

⇒ Volume = 2816 cm³

**∴ The correct answer is 2816 cm³.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Curved Surface Area of Cylinder

The curved surface area is calculated as 2 × π × r × h, representing the outer lateral surface.

Total Surface Area of Cylinder

The total surface area includes the top and bottom circular bases, calculated as 2 × π × r × (r + h).

Volume of a Cone

A cone with the same base radius and height has exactly one-third the volume of the cylinder: (1 ÷ 3) × π × r² × h.
</p

questions.question: Seven years ago, Prachi was four times as old as her daughter was at that time. Four years from now, Prachi will be two-and-a-half times as old as her daughter would then be. Find the sum of the present ages (in years) of Prachi and her daughter.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of ages (Prachi : Daughter) 7 years ago = 4 : 1 (Difference = 3 parts)

Ratio of ages 4 years from now = 2.5 : 1 = 5 : 2 (Difference = 3 parts)

Since differences are equal, 1 ratio part = Total time gap = 7 + 4 = 11 years.

Sum of ages 7 years ago = 4 + 1 = 5 parts = 5 × 11 = 55 years.

Sum of present ages = 55 + (7 × 2) = 69 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 69 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Let Prachi's present age be P and her daughter's present age be D.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b37005fc5c1f21e48554d37696f5c07685c4bd8587dc270d31a3266db90be907.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Seven years ago: P − 7 = 4 × (D − 7)

⇒ P − 4D = −28 + 7

⇒ P − 4D = −21 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ Four years from now: P + 4 = 2.5 × (D + 4)

⇒ P − 2.5D = 10 − 4

⇒ P − 2.5D = 6 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Subtracting Equation 1 from Equation 2:

⇒ (P − 2.5D) − (P − 4D) = 6 − (−21)

⇒ 1.5D = 27

⇒ D = 18 years

⇒ Substitute D = 18 in Equation 1:

⇒ P − 4 × 18 = −21

⇒ P − 72 = −21 ⇒ P = 51 years

⇒ Sum of present ages = P + D = 51 + 18 = 69 years

**∴ The correct answer is 69 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two individuals remains constant at any point in time. This is a fundamental concept used to balance ratio parts in age-related problems.

Sum of Ages Shift

If the sum of present ages of n people is S, then t years ago, their sum was S − nt, and t years later, it will be S + nt.

Ratio Balancing Method

If the difference between two quantities is unchanged, multiply the ratios by suitable integers to make the difference in ratio parts equal. Then each ratio part can be directly equated to the real-world value.
</p

questions.question: From a circle with the radius of 15.75 cm, a sector with the arc length of 11 cm is cut off. Find the area (in cm²) of this sector.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When both the arc length and the radius of a sector are given, the area can be calculated directly without finding the central angle.

Area = ¹⁄₂ × Arc Length × Radius

⇒ Area = ¹⁄₂ × 11 × 15.75

⇒ Area = 5.5 × 15.75 = 86.625 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 86.625 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Radius of the circle, r = 15.75 cm

Arc length of the sector, l = 11 cm

**Formula Used:**

Area of a sector = ¹⁄₂ × l × r

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b05fabf871411cd78e883eecd297a576c23d6cfb2d845dcff96815387b57eb4b.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Area = ¹⁄₂ × 11 × 15.75

⇒ Area = 5.5 × 15.75

⇒ Area = 86.625 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 86.625 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Area of a Sector (When central angle is given)

Area = (θ ÷ 360°) × πr², where θ is the central angle.

Arc Length (When central angle is given)

Arc length (l) = (θ ÷ 360°) × 2πr

Perimeter of a Sector

Perimeter = l + 2r (sum of the arc length and two radii)

Area of a Segment of a Circle

Area of Segment = Area of the Corresponding Sector − Area of the Triangle formed by the radii and the chord.
</p

questions.question:
Simplify:

frac{(8.3)³ + (9.2)³ + (6.1)³ - 3 times 8.3 times 9.2 times 6.1} {(8.3)² + (9.2)² + (6.1)² - 8.3 times 9.2 - 9.2 times 6.1 - 6.1 times 8.3}
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

The given expression follows the direct algebraic identity:

(a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc) ÷ (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca) = a + b + c

Here, a = 8.3, b = 9.2, and c = 6.1

Value = 8.3 + 9.2 + 6.1 = 23.6

**∴ The correct answer is 23.6.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: (8.3³ + 9.2³ + 6.1³ − 3 × 8.3 × 9.2 × 6.1) ÷ (8.3² + 9.2² + 6.1² − 8.3 × 9.2 − 9.2 × 6.1 − 6.1 × 8.3)

**Formula Used:**

a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc = (a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let a = 8.3, b = 9.2, and c = 6.1

⇒ Substituting these variables, the expression becomes:

⇒ (a³ + b³ + c³ − 3abc) ÷ (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

⇒ [(a + b + c)(a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)] ÷ (a² + b² + c² − ab − bc − ca)

⇒ The common polynomial terms cancel out, leaving:

⇒ a + b + c

⇒ 8.3 + 9.2 + 6.1

⇒ 23.6

**∴ The correct answer is 23.6.**

**__Additional Information__**

Conditional Identity

If a + b + c = 0, then the standard identity simplifies to a³ + b³ + c³ = 3abc.

Algebraic Identity for Squares

(a + b + c)² = a² + b² + c² + 2(ab + bc + ca)

Algebraic Identity for Cubes

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) and a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)
</p

questions.question: If tan (t) = 1/3, what is the value of sec (t)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Using the fundamental trigonometric identity: sec²(t) = 1 + tan²(t)

⇒ sec²(t) = 1 + (1 / 3)² = 1 + 1 / 9 = 10 / 9

⇒ sec(t) = √(10 / 9) = √10 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is √10 / 3.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

tan(t) = 1 / 3

**Formula Used:**

tan(t) = Perpendicular / Base

sec(t) = Hypotenuse / Base

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Perpendicular² + Base²

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6928b471ceb54a39c3ca280f939d897cbb4ce6b7a14e5e81f3e384e4fd0bcc24.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ By comparing the ratio, let Perpendicular = 1 and Base = 3

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(1² + 3²)

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(1 + 9) = √10

⇒ sec(t) = Hypotenuse / Base

⇒ sec(t) = √10 / 3

**∴ The correct answer is √10 / 3.**

**__Additional Information__**

Trigonometric Identities

The three primary Pythagorean identities are: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1, sec²θ − tan²θ = 1, and cosec²θ − cot²θ = 1.

Pythagoras Theorem

In a right-angled triangle, the square of the hypotenuse is equal to the sum of the squares of its base and perpendicular: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular².

Trigonometric Ratios

For an angle t in a right triangle: tan(t) = Perpendicular ÷ Base, cos(t) = Base ÷ Hypotenuse, and sec(t) is the reciprocal of cos(t) ⇒ Hypotenuse ÷ Base.
</p

questions.question: The points P and S are on the same side of the line segment QR, such that angle PQR = 90circ, angle SRQ = 90circ and PQ = SR. Select the correct statement.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Identify the given matching components between the two triangles directly.

We are given two equal sides (PQ = SR) and one common side (QR = RQ).

The angle exactly between these sides is given as equal (∠PQR = ∠SRQ = 90°).

Since the equal angle is perfectly included between the equal sides, the SAS (Side-Angle-Side) criterion applies.

RHS does not apply here because the hypotenuses (PR and SQ) are not given as equal initially.

**∴ The correct answer is ∆PQR ≅ ∆SRQ by SAS.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Points P and S are on the same side of the line segment QR.

∠PQR = 90°

∠SRQ = 90°

PQ = SR

questions.question: The marked price of an article is 26% more than its cost price. If a discount of 32% is given, what will be the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

We can use the successive percentage change formula: Net Change % = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100

Here, Markup (a) = +26% and Discount (b) = −32%

Net Change = 26 − 32 + (26 × −32) ÷ 100

Net Change = −6 − 8.32 = −14.32%

The negative sign indicates a loss of 14.32%.

**∴ The correct answer is 14.32%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup percentage = 26%

Discount percentage = 32%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9e5547b56a4c0931d77de5edb393582f9f023aacc961e23841316c1b96158e2f.png] 

**Formula Used:**

MP = CP × (1 + Markup% ÷ 100)

SP = MP × (1 − Discount% ÷ 100)

Loss% = [(CP − SP) ÷ CP] × 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let Cost Price (CP) = 100

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 26 = 126

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 126 × (1 − 32 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 126 × 0.68

⇒ SP = 85.68

⇒ Loss = CP − SP = 100 − 85.68 = 14.32

⇒ Loss % = (14.32 ÷ 100) × 100 = 14.32%

**∴ The correct answer is 14.32%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is sequentially changed by a% and then by b%, the net percentage change is given by the formula: Net % = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Markup and Discount Relation

The final Profit or Loss percentage is simply the successive application of the Markup percentage and the Discount percentage. Using the successive formula: Profit/Loss % = Markup% − Discount% − (Markup% × Discount%) ÷ 100.

Selling Price Link

The Selling Price acts as a bridge between the Cost Price and Marked Price. SP = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss)% and SP = MP × (100 − Discount)%.
</p

questions.question: Simplify the following. (sin³A - cos³A)/(sin A - cos A), where A is an acute angle.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Using the algebraic difference of cubes identity: x³ − y³ = (x − y)(x² + y² + xy)

Substitute x = sinA and y = cosA into the given expression directly:

⇒ [(sinA − cosA)(sin²A + cos²A + sinA × cosA)] ÷ (sinA − cosA)

⇒ sin²A + cos²A + sinA × cosA

⇒ 1 + sinA cosA

**∴ The correct answer is 1 + sinA cosA.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Expression: (sin³A − cos³A) ÷ (sinA − cosA)

**Formula Used:**

a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²)

sin²A + cos²A = 1

**Calculation:**

⇒ Expand the numerator using the difference of cubes formula.

⇒ Numerator = (sinA − cosA)(sin²A + cos²A + sinA × cosA)

⇒ Substitute this expansion back into the fraction:

⇒ [(sinA − cosA)(sin²A + cos²A + sinA × cosA)] ÷ (sinA − cosA)

⇒ The common term (sinA − cosA) cancels out from the numerator and the denominator.

⇒ We are left with: sin²A + cos²A + sinA × cosA

⇒ Applying the basic trigonometric identity sin²A + cos²A = 1.

⇒ 1 + sinA cosA

**∴ The correct answer is 1 + sinA cosA.**

**__Additional Information__**

Sum of Cubes Identity

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²). This is extremely useful for expressions like (sin³A + cos³A) ÷ (sinA + cosA) which easily simplifies to 1 − sinA cosA.

Basic Trigonometric Identities

1 + tan²A = sec²A and 1 + cot²A = cosec²A. These fundamental identities along with sin²A + cos²A = 1 are frequently used to simplify complex trigonometric fractions.

Value Substitution Strategy

For algebraic or trigonometric simplifications where options are in terms of functions, substituting standard angles like A = 30° or 60° (avoiding values where the denominator becomes zero) can help quickly verify the correct option during exams.
</p

questions.question: A right-angled isosceles triangle has an area of 50 square units. Its hypotenuse is (in units):
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For a right-angled isosceles triangle, the area can be directly related to its hypotenuse (h) using the relation: Area = h² ÷ 4

⇒ 50 = h² ÷ 4

⇒ h² = 200

⇒ h = √200 = 10√2

**∴ The correct answer is 10√2 units.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Area of the right-angled isosceles triangle = 50 sq. units

**Formula Used:**

Area of a triangle = (1 ÷ 2) × base × height

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse = √(base² + height²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64d4c6abae86526402af13df84876ac2a747e43c4584bdb0ab477a359a9759ec.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the equal sides (base and height) be 'a' units.

⇒ Area = (1 ÷ 2) × a × a = 50

⇒ a² = 50 × 2

⇒ a² = 100

⇒ a = 10 units

⇒ Now, applying Pythagoras Theorem to find the hypotenuse:

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(a² + a²)

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(10² + 10²)

⇒ Hypotenuse = √(100 + 100)

⇒ Hypotenuse = √200

⇒ Hypotenuse = 10√2 units

**∴ The correct answer is 10√2 units.**

**__Additional Information__**

Right-angled Isosceles Triangle Properties

The angles in a right-angled isosceles triangle are always 90°, 45° and 45°. The ratio of its sides is consistently 1 : 1 : √2.

Perimeter

The perimeter of a right-angled isosceles triangle with equal sides 'a' is given by P = a(2 + √2).

Hypotenuse-Area Relationship

If the length of the hypotenuse is 'h', the area can be easily determined directly as Area = h² ÷ 4 without calculating the lengths of the legs.
</p

questions.question: A person earns ₹16,000 per month and spends 80% of his income and saves the remaining amount. If his income increases by 20% and expenditure by 10%, find the percentage of increase in his savings.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Expenditure : Savings = 80% : 20% = 4 : 1 (Total = 5 parts).

By weighted average rule: Overall Change = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂)

⇒ 20 = (4 × 10 + 1 × x) ÷ 5

⇒ 100 = 40 + x ⇒ x = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Income = ₹16,000

Expenditure = 80% of Income

Income increase = 20%

Expenditure increase = 10%

**Formula Used:**

Income = Expenditure + Savings

Percentage Increase = [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/154b0c6961f38d02c61af6772966a30eda890086fcee3c54dbf8440305b437a2.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Expenditure = (80 ÷ 100) × 16000 = ₹12,800

⇒ Initial Savings = 16000 − 12800 = ₹3,200

⇒ New Income = 16000 + (20% of 16000) = 16000 + 3200 = ₹19,200

⇒ New Expenditure = 12800 + (10% of 12800) = 12800 + 1280 = ₹14,080

⇒ New Savings = 19200 − 14080 = ₹5,120

⇒ Increase in Savings = 5120 − 3200 = ₹1,920

⇒ Percentage Increase in Savings = (1920 ÷ 3200) × 100 = 60%

**∴ The correct answer is 60%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

It measures the difference between a new value and an old value as a percentage of the old value: Percentage Change = [(New Value − Old Value) ÷ Old Value] × 100.

Successive Percentage

When a value undergoes two consecutive percentage changes of a% and b%, the effective overall percentage change is given by: Net Change = a + b + (a × b) ÷ 100.

Weighted Average (Mixture Concept)

When a base quantity is divided into two parts, the overall percentage change is equivalent to the weighted average of the changes in the individual parts: Overall Change = (w₁x₁ + w₂x₂) ÷ (w₁ + w₂).

questions.question: Without doing the actual division, find the remainder when 28735429 is divided by 9.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To find the remainder when a number is divided by 9, apply the casting out nines technique.

Cancel out any digits or groups of digits in 28735429 that sum to 9.

Cancel 9, the pair (2 + 7), and the pair (5 + 4).

The remaining digits are 8, 3, and 2.

Sum of remaining digits = 8 + 3 + 2 = 13 ⇒ 1 + 3 = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number = 28735429

Divisor = 9

**Method Used:**

The remainder of a number divided by 9 is the same as the remainder of the sum of its digits divided by 9.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of digits = 2 + 8 + 7 + 3 + 5 + 4 + 2 + 9

⇒ Sum of digits = 40

⇒ Divide 40 by 9: 40 = 9 × 4 + 4

⇒ The remainder obtained is 4.

⇒ Alternatively, the sum of digits of 40 = 4 + 0 = 4.

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Divisibility Rule of 3

A number is completely divisible by 3 if the sum of its digits is divisible by 3. The remainder obtained is the same as dividing the sum of digits by 3.

Divisibility Rule of 11

A number is divisible by 11 if the difference between the sum of digits at odd places and the sum of digits at even places is 0 or a multiple of 11.

Divisibility Rule of 8

A number is divisible by 8 if the number formed by its last three digits is exactly divisible by 8.

Digital Root Concept

The single-digit value obtained by repeatedly summing the digits of a number is its digital root, which gives the exact remainder when the number is divided by 9.
</p

questions.question:
The angles of triangle are such that one is average of other two, then the angles are:

1) (pi)/(6) (pi)/(3) (pi)/(2) 2) (pi)/(3) (pi)/(3) (pi)/(2) 3) (pi)/(6) (pi)/(3) (pi)/(4) 4) (pi)/(2) (pi)/(2) (pi)/(3)
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

If the angles of a triangle are in an Arithmetic Progression (i.e., one angle is the average of the other two), the middle angle is always π/3 (or 60°).

Checking the given options, only the first set contains π/3 and sums to π radians.

Sum = π/6 + π/3 + π/2 = π.

Average of π/6 and π/2 = (π/6 + π/2) ÷ 2 = (4π/6) ÷ 2 = π/3.

**∴ The correct answer is π/6, π/3, π/2.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

One angle of a triangle is the arithmetic average of the other two angles.

**Formula Used:**

Sum of interior angles in a triangle = π radians.

Average = (Sum of values) ÷ Number of values

 

 

 

 

 A
 B
 C
 π/6
 π/3
 π/2
 Right-Angled Triangle with Angles in A.P.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the three angles of the triangle be A, B, and C.

⇒ According to the given condition, let B be the average of A and C: B = (A + C) ÷ 2

⇒ Multiplying by 2, we get: 2B = A + C

⇒ We know the sum property of triangles: A + B + C = π

⇒ Substituting A + C = 2B in the sum equation:

⇒ B + (A + C) = π

⇒ B + 2B = π

⇒ 3B = π → B = π/3

⇒ Since B = π/3, the remaining sum is A + C = π − π/3 = 2π/3

⇒ Checking the first set of angles from the options: π/6, π/3, π/2

⇒ Here, the middle angle is π/3. Sum of the other two angles = π/6 + π/2 = π/6 + 3π/6 = 4π/6 = 2π/3.

⇒ The first set identically matches all our derived geometric conditions.

**∴ The correct answer is π/6, π/3, π/2.**

**__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Progression of Angles

When the angles of a triangle are in an Arithmetic Progression (A.P.), the middle angle is always exactly 60° (or π/3 radians), unconditionally regardless of what the other two adjacent angles are.

Sum of Angles Property

The sum of interior angles in any Euclidean planar triangle is strictly equal to 180° (which is algebraically equivalent to π radians). Universal formula: A + B + C = π.

Radian and Degree Conversion

To convert a measurement from radians to degrees, we multiply the given radian value by 180°/π. For example, π/6 × (180°/π) = 30° and π/2 × (180°/π) = 90°.
</p

questions.question: At present, A is thrice as old as B. C is 5 years elder than B. The sum of the ages of A, B, C is 75 years. The ratio of the age of B five years ago to the age of A three years from now is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let B's present age be x.

Then A = 3x, and C = x + 5.

Total sum: 3x + x + x + 5 = 75 ⇒ 5x = 70 ⇒ x = 14.

Present ages: B = 14 years, A = 3 × 14 = 42 years.

Ratio of (B − 5) to (A + 3) = (14 − 5) : (42 + 3) = 9 : 45 = 1 : 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A is thrice as old as B ⇒ A = 3B

C is 5 years elder than B ⇒ C = B + 5

Sum of ages of A, B, and C = 75 years

**Formula Used:**

Past age = Present age − Number of years

Future age = Present age + Number of years

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/834e0a68b1df7354e81c530fea97cfc8d52f66928e3cfa8235386c603afb06fa.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the present age of B be x.

⇒ Present age of A = 3x

⇒ Present age of C = x + 5

According to the given condition, sum of their ages is 75:

⇒ 3x + x + (x + 5) = 75

⇒ 5x + 5 = 75

⇒ 5x = 70

⇒ x = 14

Now, calculate the required ages:

⇒ Present age of B = 14 years

⇒ Present age of A = 3 × 14 = 42 years

⇒ Age of B five years ago = 14 − 5 = 9 years

⇒ Age of A three years from now = 42 + 3 = 45 years

Find the required ratio:

⇒ Required Ratio = 9 : 45

⇒ Required Ratio = 1 : 5

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 5.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Past and Future Ages

If the present age is x, then age n years ago is (x − n) and age n years from now is (x + n).

Constant Difference

The difference between the ages of two persons always remains constant irrespective of past, present, or future times.

Ratio of Ages

If the ratio of present ages of A and B is a : b, then their actual ages can be assumed as ax and bx respectively, where x is a common constant multiplier.
</p

questions.question: If x varies inversely as y and x = 2 when y = 6, then the value of y when x = 3 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For inverse variation, the product of the two variables is always constant.

x₁ × y₁ = x₂ × y₂

2 × 6 = 3 × y

12 = 3 × y ⇒ y = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

x varies inversely as y.

When x = 2, y = 6.

**Formula Used:**

If x ∝ 1/y, then x × y = k (where k is a constant)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9b7d68adfbbec74f7ccec7c65344973e9c110d0a7f3018f30fa22d0602abfebe.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, find the constant k using the initial values.

⇒ k = 2 × 6 = 12

⇒ Now, substitute x = 3 and k = 12 into the relation.

⇒ 3 × y = 12

⇒ y = 12 ÷ 3

⇒ y = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Variation

If two quantities change in the same proportion, they are in direct variation. The ratio between them remains constant: x ÷ y = k.

Joint Variation

Occurs when a variable is directly proportional to the product of two or more other variables. Example formula: x = k × y × z.

Compound Ratio

The ratio obtained by multiplying the antecedent parts together and the consequent parts together. If a:b and c:d are two ratios, the compound ratio is (a × c) : (b × d).
</p

questions.question: If a sum of ₹5,000 is taken at a simple rate of interest of 15% per annum for 3 years and another sum of ₹8,000 is taken at a simple interest of 12% per annum for 4 years, the positive difference of the interests paid is:

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective interest percentage for the first sum = 15% × 3 = 45%

Interest on the first sum = 45% of 5000 = ₹2,250

Effective interest percentage for the second sum = 12% × 4 = 48%

Interest on the second sum = 48% of 8000 = ₹3,840

Positive difference = 3840 − 2250 = 1590

**∴ The correct answer is ₹1,590.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

P₁ = ₹5,000, R₁ = 15%, T₁ = 3 years

P₂ = ₹8,000, R₂ = 12%, T₂ = 4 years

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI₁ = 50 × 45 = ₹2,250

⇒ SI₂ = (8000 × 12 × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ SI₂ = 80 × 48 = ₹3,840

⇒ Difference = SI₂ − SI₁

⇒ Difference = 3840 − 2250 = ₹1,590

Compound Interest Formula

The accumulated amount over T years is calculated using the formula A = P(1 + R/100)T.

SI vs CI Difference

For exactly 2 years, the difference between CI and SI on the same principal is P(R/100)². For 3 years, the exact difference formula is P(R/100)² × (3 + R/100).

Rule of 72

A well-known approximation stating that the time needed to double an investment at a compound rate of R% is roughly 72 ÷ R years.

questions.question: Varun and Sandeep started for a car race from the same point, in the same direction and at the same time on a circular track of length 1635 m with the speeds of 90 km/h and 108 km/h, respectively. After how much time (in s) will they meet again for the first time?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Relative speed (same direction) = 108 − 90 = 18 km/h

Relative speed in m/s = 18 × (5/18) = 5 m/s

Time to meet = Distance ÷ Relative speed

Time to meet = 1635 ÷ 5 = 327 s

**∴ The correct answer is 327 s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of the circular track = 1635 m

Speed of Varun = 90 km/h

Speed of Sandeep = 108 km/h

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c9ae52f2f06fd1987c4e94a36dbf802929c1466ca3c897098f772c34b395131f.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time to meet for the first time = Track Length ÷ Relative Speed

Relative speed (same direction) = S₁ − S₂

**Calculations:**

⇒ Speed of Varun = 90 × (5/18) = 25 m/s

⇒ Speed of Sandeep = 108 × (5/18) = 30 m/s

⇒ Relative speed = 30 − 25 = 5 m/s

⇒ Time to meet = 1635 ÷ 5 = 327 s

**∴ The correct answer is 327 s.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting for the first time anywhere on the track

When moving in the same direction: Time = Distance ÷ (S₁ − S₂). When moving in opposite directions: Time = Distance ÷ (S₁ + S₂).

Meeting at the starting point

The time taken to meet at the starting point for the first time is the LCM of the times taken by each individual to complete one full round.

Relative Speed

Relative speed is the speed of a moving object with respect to another. If they move in the same direction, speeds subtract; if opposite, speeds add.

Unit Conversion

To convert km/h to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/h, multiply by 18/5.
</p

questions.question: Pipes M, N and S can fill a tank in 25, 50 and 100 minutes, respectively. Initially, pipes N and S are kept open for 10 minutes, and then pipe N is shut while pipe M is opened. Pipe S is closed 15 minutes before the tank overflows. How much time (in minutes) will it take to fill the tank if the three pipes work in this pattern?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total capacity = LCM(25, 50, 100) = 100 units ⇒ Efficiency: M = 4, N = 2, S = 1.

Let the total time taken to fill the tank be T minutes.

Pipe N works for exactly 10 mins, S works for (T − 15) mins, and M works for (T − 10) mins.

⇒ (10 × 2) + 1 × (T − 15) + 4 × (T − 10) = 100

⇒ 5T − 35 = 100 ⇒ 5T = 135 ⇒ T = 27 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 27 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by pipe M to fill the tank = 25 minutes

Time taken by pipe N to fill the tank = 50 minutes

Time taken by pipe S to fill the tank = 100 minutes

**Calculations:**

 
 

 **Pipe**
 **Time (min)**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**
 
 

 M

 N

 S

⇒ Let the total time taken to fill the tank completely be T minutes.

⇒ Initially, pipes N and S are opened. After 10 minutes, pipe N is shut, which means pipe N operates for exactly 10 minutes.

⇒ Pipe M is opened after 10 minutes and continues until the end, so it operates for (T − 10) minutes.

⇒ Pipe S starts from the beginning but is closed 15 minutes before the tank is full, meaning it operates for (T − 15) minutes.

⇒ Total Work = (Work by N) + (Work by S) + (Work by M)

⇒ (10 × 2) + 1 × (T − 15) + 4 × (T − 10) = 100

⇒ 20 + T − 15 + 4T − 40 = 100

⇒ 5T − 35 = 100

⇒ 5T = 135

⇒ T = 27 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 27 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Concept

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours, its efficiency (the fraction of the tank filled in 1 hour) is 1/x. Always compute Total Capacity using the LCM of individual times.

Leaving/Joining Work Strategy

Whenever pipes open or close at different intervals, assign a variable for the total filling time (T) and define the operating duration of each pipe in terms of T. Sum up their individual work outputs and equate them to the Total Capacity.

Negative Work (Outlet Pipes)

If a pipe empties the tank, its efficiency is treated as negative. The total work equation becomes: Total work = Positive work − Negative work.
</p

questions.question: The average temperature of a city for the first sixteen days of January is 22ºC, and the average temperature for the last sixteen days of the same month is 26ºC. If the average temperature for the entire month is 24ºC, what is the temperature on the sixteenth day?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Average temperature of 31 days in January = 24ºC

Total deviation for first 16 days = 16 × (22 − 24) = −32

Total deviation for last 16 days = 16 × (26 − 24) = +32

Net deviation = −32 + 32 = 0

Temperature on the 16th day = Average + Net Deviation = 24 + 0 = 24ºC

**∴ The correct answer is 24ºC.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Average temperature of first 16 days = 22ºC

Average temperature of last 16 days = 26ºC

Average temperature of the entire month (31 days) = 24ºC

**Formula Used:**

Temperature of overlapped day = (Sum of part 1) + (Sum of part 2) − (Total sum)

 
 
 First 16 days: 22ºC
 
 
 
 Last 16 days: 26ºC
 
 
 
 
• 
 
• 
 16th Day

 
 
 Entire Month (31 days): 24ºC

**Calculations:**

⇒ Sum of temperatures of first 16 days = 16 × 22 = 352

⇒ Sum of temperatures of last 16 days = 16 × 26 = 416

⇒ Total sum of temperatures for the entire month = 31 × 24 = 744

⇒ Temperature on the 16th day = (352 + 416) − 744

⇒ Temperature on the 16th day = 768 − 744 = 24

**∴ The correct answer is 24ºC.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Arithmetic Mean (Average)

The average is the sum of all values divided by the total number of values. Formula: Average = Sum ÷ Count.

Overlapping Groups Principle

When two subsets overlap on a single item (like the middle day in a month), the value of the overlapping item is determined by adding the sum of both subsets and subtracting the total sum of all items.

Deviation Method

The sum of total deviations from the exact average is always zero. This property can be used as a smart shortcut to quickly find missing or overlapping values by balancing the positive and negative net deviations against the base average.
</p
